nodes.title: the Duthtarn signature
nodes.statement: The Duthtarn system concerns objects called tezkas. There are exactly 3 of them: lumwren, vorzel, opalfex. Two operations are written >< and |. One relation is written <~, read as "covers".

nodes.title: the Duthtarn combination tables
nodes.statement: The value of x >< y for every pair of tezkas is fixed by the table of the first operation, and likewise for |. The pairs standing in the <~ relation are listed in full.

nodes.title: closure under the first operation
nodes.statement: For all tezkas x and y, x >< y is again a tezka.

nodes.title: association of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all tezkas x, y, z: (x >< y) >< z = x >< (y >< z).

nodes.title: commutation of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all tezkas x and y: x >< y = y >< x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a tezka lumwren with lumwren >< x = x >< lumwren = x for every x.

nodes.title: reversal under the first operation
nodes.statement: For every tezka x there is a tezka y with x >< y = y >< x = lumwren.

nodes.title: cancellation in the first operation
nodes.statement: For all tezkas x, y, z: if x >< y = x >< z then y = z.

nodes.title: closure under the second operation
nodes.statement: For all tezkas x and y, x | y is again a tezka.

nodes.title: association of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all tezkas x, y, z: (x | y) | z = x | (y | z).

nodes.title: commutation of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all tezkas x and y: x | y = y | x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the second operation
nodes.statement: There is a tezka vorzel with vorzel | x = x for every x.

nodes.title: spreading of the second operation over the first
nodes.statement: For all tezkas x, y, z: x | (y >< z) = (x | y) >< (x | z), and the same on the right.

nodes.title: reflexivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For every tezka x: x <~ x.

nodes.title: transitivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For all tezkas x, y, z: if x <~ y and y <~ z then x <~ z.

nodes.title: comparability of every pair
nodes.statement: For all tezkas x and y, at least one of x <~ y and y <~ x holds.

nodes.title: agreement of the relation with the first operation
nodes.statement: For all tezkas x, y, z: if x <~ y then (z >< x) <~ (z >< y) and (x >< z) <~ (y >< z).

nodes.title: agreement of the relation with the second operation
nodes.statement: For all tezkas x, y, z: if x <~ y then (z | x) <~ (z | y) and (x | z) <~ (y | z).

nodes.title: the system does not have self combination under the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every tezka x: x >< x = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = vorzel, value = opalfex, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have an absorbing object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is no tezka z with z >< x = x >< z = z for every tezka x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case reason = no absorbing element, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have self combination under the second operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every tezka x: x | x = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = opalfex, value = vorzel, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have the absorption pair
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all tezkas x and y: x >< (x | y) = x and x | (x >< y) = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = vorzel, y = vorzel, value = opalfex, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have antisymmetry of the relation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all tezkas x and y: if x <~ y and y <~ x then x = y.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = lumwren, y = vorzel, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: xilvash tezkas
nodes.statement: A tezka x is called xilvash when x >< x = x.

nodes.title: tezkas that espanak
nodes.statement: Two tezkas x and y are said to espanak when x >< y = y >< x.

nodes.title: qenduth collections
nodes.statement: A collection S of tezkas is qenduth when x >< y belongs to S for every pair x, y drawn from S.

nodes.title: the tarnopal of a tezka
nodes.statement: The tarnopal of a tezka x is the collection of tezkas y for which x <~ y holds.

nodes.title: the yukvex
nodes.statement: The tezka lumwren is called the yukvex of the system. It is the unique tezka that leaves every tezka unchanged under ><.

nodes.title: the drilorn
nodes.statement: The drilorn of the system is the collection of tezkas that espanak with every tezka.

nodes.title: the lorngrix
nodes.statement: The lorngrix is the collection of all xilvash tezkas.

nodes.title: the nyrpon of a tezka
nodes.statement: The nyrpon of a tezka x, written [x], is the smallest qenduth collection that contains x.

nodes.title: a hurnhob
nodes.statement: A tezka f is a hurnhob when f <~ y holds for every tezka y, that is, when the tarnopal of f is the whole system.

nodes.title: hobthra tezkas
nodes.statement: A tezka x is hobthra when x >< x equals the yukvex.

nodes.title: the tezzam of a tezka
nodes.statement: A tezzam of a tezka x is a tezka y with x >< y = y >< x = lumwren.

nodes.title: the pyryuk of a tezka
nodes.statement: The pyryuk of a tezka x is the number of tezkas in its nyrpon [x].

nodes.title: the duthquil
nodes.statement: The duthquil of the system is the collection of tezkas whose pyryuk is largest.

nodes.title: thrahob pairs
nodes.statement: Two distinct tezkas x and y form a thrahob pair when x <~ y and y <~ x both hold, that is, when each lies in the tarnopal of the other.

nodes.title: the yukvex is the only one of its kind
nodes.statement: There is exactly one tezka e with e >< x = x >< e = x for every tezka x.

verification.domain: every object paired with every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose e and f both leave every tezka unchanged.
Then e >< f = f, reading e as neutral on the left.
And e >< f = e, reading f as neutral on the right.
So e = f, and the two suppositions describe the same object.

nodes.title: the yukvex lies in the drilorn
nodes.statement: The yukvex espanaks with every tezka.

verification.domain: the anchor against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let e be the yukvex and x any tezka.
Then e >< x = x and x >< e = x.
So e >< x = x >< e, which is what it means to espanak.
Since x was arbitrary, e belongs to the drilorn.

nodes.title: a tezka has only one tezzam
nodes.statement: For every tezka x there is exactly one tezzam of x.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y and z both be partners of x.
Then y = y >< (x >< z) = (y >< x) >< z.
Both bracketed products collapse to the neutral object.
So y = z.

nodes.title: a hobthra tezka is its own tezzam
nodes.statement: If x >< x is the yukvex then the tezzam of x is x itself.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x be hobthra, so x >< x is the yukvex.
That is exactly the condition for x to be a partner of x.
Partners are unique, so no other object can be one.

nodes.title: the drilorn is qenduth
nodes.statement: If x and y both espanak with every tezka, then so does x >< y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y lie in the drilorn and let z be any tezka.
Then (x >< y) >< z = x >< (y >< z).
Move z past y, then past x, using that each espanaks with everything.
So x >< y espanaks with z, and the drilorn is qenduth.

nodes.title: the nyrpon of a tezka is qenduth
nodes.statement: For every tezka x, the collection [x] is qenduth.

verification.domain: every object, then every pair inside its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is built by taking x and closing under ><.
Closing under an operation is exactly the sealing condition.
The carrier is finite, so the closure stops after finitely many rounds.

nodes.title: the nyrpon is contained in every qenduth collection
nodes.statement: If S is qenduth and contains x, then S contains all of [x].

verification.domain: every sealed collection against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every member of [x] is reached from x by finitely many applications of the operation.
A sealed S containing x is closed under each of those applications.
So each member of [x] is in S, by induction on the number of applications.

nodes.title: a tezka is xilvash exactly when its pyryuk is one
nodes.statement: x >< x = x holds if and only if [x] contains x alone.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: If x >< x = x then {x} is already closed under ><.
So [x] = {x} and the pyryuk is one.
Conversely a span of one object must contain x >< x, which is then x.

nodes.title: the pyryuk divides the number of tezkas
nodes.statement: For every tezka x, the pyryuk of x divides 3.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is a qenduth collection.
Its size is the pyryuk of x.
The claim is that this size always divides 3.

nodes.title: the nyrpon of a drilorn tezka stays in the drilorn
nodes.statement: If x lies in the drilorn then every tezka of [x] lies in the drilorn.

verification.domain: every object of the core, then its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The drilorn is qenduth.
[x] is the smallest qenduth collection containing x.
A smallest such collection sits inside any other, and the drilorn is one.

nodes.title: the lorngrix is qenduth
nodes.statement: If x and y are both xilvash then so is x >< y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the ridge
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y be xilvash.
The claim asks whether (x >< y) >< (x >< y) returns x >< y.
Whether it does is settled by running the operation table on every such pair.

nodes.title: combining on the left never merges two tezkas
nodes.statement: For every tezka a, the assignment x to a >< x sends distinct tezkas to distinct tezkas.

verification.domain: every object translated by every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose a >< x = a >< y.
Cancellation on the left gives x = y.
So the assignment is injective, and being injective on a finite carrier it is onto.

nodes.title: tarnopals are nested along the relation
nodes.statement: If y lies in the tarnopal of x, then the tarnopal of y is contained in the tarnopal of x.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y satisfy x <~ y and let z satisfy y <~ z.
Transitivity gives x <~ z.
So every member of the tarnopal of y is a member of that of x.

nodes.title: the system has a hurnhob
nodes.statement: Some tezka hurnhobs the whole system.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every pair is comparable, so the relation orders the objects into a line.
The claim is that the line has a bottom.
The carrier is finite, so the search over candidates terminates.

nodes.title: the relation survives combination on the right
nodes.statement: If x <~ y then (x >< z) <~ (y >< z) for every tezka z.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y lie in the tarnopal of x.
Compatibility applies the operation to both sides at once.
Nothing else is needed, since z was arbitrary.

nodes.title: every tezka lies in the drilorn
nodes.statement: Every pair of tezkas espanaks.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The drilorn is defined by espanaking with everything.
The claim is that x >< y = y >< x for every pair.
That is settled by scanning the table for a pair that disagrees.

nodes.title: where every tezka is xilvash breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: x >< x = x for every tezka x.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = vorzel, value = opalfex, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: some tezka reaches every other
nodes.statement: There is a tezka whose nyrpon is the whole system.

verification.domain: every object and its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Compute [x] for each tezka in turn.
The claim is that some pyryuk equals 3.
The search runs over finitely many objects, so it settles.

nodes.title: the relation reads the same in both directions
nodes.statement: If x <~ y then y <~ x.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Symmetry would mean y lies in the tarnopal of x exactly when x lies in that of y.
The listed pairs settle it directly.

nodes.title: where the yukvex swallows everything breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: e >< x equals the yukvex for every tezka x.

verification.domain: the anchor against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case anchor = lumwren, x = vorzel, value = vorzel, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the second operation keeps the drilorn intact
nodes.statement: If x and y lie in the drilorn then so does x | y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The drilorn is already qenduth under ><.
The second operation is defined on every pair.
The claim is that | respects the drilorn as well.
